name: Ad Lifecycle Races
note: Gate 2-10 reads the source and checks what the screen claims; it cannot see a defect that only appears when two awaits interleave, because the code reads correctly in either order. Both bugs here came from cross-review rather than from any gate, and both were invisible to a player: an ad that never loads looks exactly like an app with no ads, and a banner that appears on the wrong screen looks like a layout bug. The gate drives the real provider against a stub plugin whose promises the test resolves by hand, so the interleaving is deterministic instead of something that shows up on one device in ten. Worth recording how the first version of this gate failed: it passed three sections while reaching none of the code under test, because Node has no import.meta.env so the ad unit ids were empty strings and showBanner returned before it ever touched init. A green that means the check could not reach its subject is the same fault as a fifty-character list wearing the name of a complete check.

mutations.name: a thrown init failure is cached for the life of the process
mutations.why: The shipped behaviour. One failed consent lookup at launch — a phone starting the app in a lift — turned ads off until the app was killed, because the rejected promise stayed in initPromise and every later call returned it. Nothing on screen said so.

mutations.name: every init failure is retried, including a declined consent
mutations.why: The overcorrection, and the reason the fix distinguishes three outcomes rather than two. Retrying a thrown error is right; retrying a user who declined means re-presenting the consent form to somebody who already said no, which is the violation this whole flow exists to prevent. The gate has to reject this as firmly as it rejects the cache.

mutations.name: showBanner does not re-check intent after awaiting init
mutations.why: The race as shipped. The banner is a native overlay pinned to the bottom of the screen, not an element inside the page, so one that arrives late does not sit in a reserved slot — it lands on top of whatever is showing now. A player who left the game screen while consent was still resolving got a banner across the settings list.

mutations.name: hideBanner records its intent only after awaiting the plugin
mutations.why: The subtler half: the flag has to be set synchronously, before any await, or an in-flight showBanner wakes up and still reads bannerWanted as true. Ordering the assignment after the native call looks equivalent and is not, which is precisely the class of mistake a source-reading gate cannot catch. Recorded as SURVIVED first: the gate awaited hideBanner to completion, so the assignment's position made no difference. A screen transition does not wait for the native hide, so section 5 holds the plugin promise open — which is what the device actually does and what makes this detectable at all.
